headline: Binance hacked: $6.3 billion in crypto stolen in record-breaking heist
summary: The world's largest crypto exchange reports a massive security breach, with withdrawals frozen as authorities attempt to recover billions in stolen assets.
details: Binance.com, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, has suffered a massive hack resulting in the theft of approximately $6.3 billion in various cryptocurrencies. Withdrawals on the platform have been suspended as the company works to address the situation.

The stolen assets include significant amounts of stablecoins like Tether (USDT) and Circle (USDC), totaling around $2.4 billion, which have been frozen by their issuers. Other stolen cryptocurrencies include Bitcoin (BTC) and Ethereum (ETH), amounting to roughly $3.2 billion.

While stablecoin issuers have taken steps to freeze the stolen funds, the fate of the remaining billions in pure cryptocurrencies remains uncertain. These funds are likely lost unless recovery mechanisms are successfully employed.

The exchange has assured users that their funds are safe and has pledged to cover all losses incurred from the breach. Binance has a SAFU (Secure Asset Fund for Users) reserve, established in 2018, which deposits 10% of trading fees to cover such security incidents.

This incident surpasses previous major crypto heists, including the $1.5 billion stolen from Bybit in February 2025. The exact method of intrusion, whether through stolen private keys or a compromised signing process, is still under investigation.

Binance is also warning users about potential phishing scams and impersonation attempts related to the hack, urging caution with any communications or offers regarding compensation or withdrawal restoration.

The exchange has assured users that their funds are safe and has pledged to cover all losses incurred from the breach. Binance has a SAFU (Secure Asset Fund for Users) reserve, established in 2018, which deposits 10% of trading fees to cover such security incidents.

headline: Boost Chrome Speed and Save Battery by Tweaking These Settings
summary: Discover how buried Chrome flags and cache clearing can dramatically improve performance and extend your Android device's battery life.
details: Google Chrome, while fast on paper, can suffer from laggy performance and excessive battery drain on Android devices. Fortunately, several hidden settings can significantly boost its speed and efficiency.

The 'Preload pages' setting, designed to speed up browsing by loading sites before you visit them, can actually slow down Chrome's initial launch and consume extra battery. Disabling it can yield noticeable improvements, especially for users who don't browse for extended periods.

GPU rasterization is another key setting. By default, Chrome uses the CPU for this process, but forcing it to use the GPU can dramatically improve page load times and overall responsiveness across various devices, including Android phones.

Clearing Chrome's cached data is a simple yet effective way to free up storage space and speed up the browser. Over time, the cache can accumulate unnecessary data from visited websites, slowing down performance.

The Experimental QUIC protocol, found in Chrome's flags menu, offers an alternative to traditional protocols like TCP and HTTP/2. Enabling it can further accelerate browsing by reducing server response times, though it may make troubleshooting network issues more complex.
